Administracion de Aeropuertos y Servicio.desc: A Bolivian state body that planned, ran and administered the country's public airports and organised national airspace and air traffic control. Supreme Decree 8019 of 21 June 1967 created it as a state body depending administratively on the Ministry of Public Works and Communications through the Sub-Secretaria de Transportes, and passed Lloyd Aereo Boliviano's aeronautical infrastructure property to it. Supreme Decree 4630 of 30 November 2021 ordered it to stop operating and be wound up.

sources.title: Decreto Supremo No 08019 de 21 de junio de 1967
Bolivia: Decreto Supremo No 4630, 30 de noviembre de 2021

Administradora Boliviana de Carreteras (.desc: The Bolivian state body responsible for planning and managing the Red Vial Fundamental, the national trunk road network. Law 3507 of 27 October 2006 set it up as an autonomous public-law entity with its own legal personality and assets, under the oversight of the Ministry of Public Works, Services and Housing. It also oversees tolls, weighbridges and vehicle-dimension control on that network, with 30 per cent of that revenue going to the departmental prefectures.

sources.title: Bolivia: Ley No 3507, 27 de octubre de 2006

NAABOL.desc: Navegacion Aerea y Aeropuertos Bolivianos (NAABOL), the Bolivian state body created by Supreme Decree 4630 of 30 November 2021, the decree that also wound up AASANA. It sits under the oversight of the Ministry of Public Works, Services and Housing and is responsible for planning aeronautical infrastructure, directing and administering the state's airports, and organising airspace and air traffic control.

sources.title: Bolivia: Decreto Supremo No 4630, 30 de noviembre de 2021

Consejo Indigena del Pueblo Tacana (CIPT.desc: The representative organisation of the Tacana indigenous people in Abel Iturralde province, La Paz department, Bolivia, founded in 1993. It is run by a directorio whose posts are a president, a vice-president and secretaries for natural resources, for land and autonomy, for economy and development, for education, health and sport, for gender, tourism and culture, and for communication and research. The Tacana I communal territory it belongs to has 20 communities, titled in part, in the municipalities of Ixiamas and San Buenaventura, and CIPTA and the Tacana women's council CIMTA both follow up the territory's titling.

CONDER - Companhia de Desenvolvimento Ur.desc: A public company (empresa publica) of the Brazilian state of Bahia, listed as such on the register of state public companies kept by Bahia's commercial registry, JUCEB, with its address on Avenida Edgar Santos in Salvador. A state decree reported in March 2015 makes it the body that carries out works and extensions on state public buildings once their cost passes limits set for each agency, and Bahia state Law 13.204 of 2014 allows the state administration secretariat to delegate the building of public facilities to it.

SEDUR - Secretaria de Desenvolvimento Ur.desc: A secretariat of the government of the Brazilian state of Bahia, based in the Centro Administrativo da Bahia, the state administrative centre in Salvador. Bahia state Law 13.204 of 11 December 2014 gives it the purpose of drawing up and carrying out state policy on urban development, housing and technical assistance to municipalities. The same law creates inside it a Superintendencia de Mobilidade for urban and intercity mobility, transport planning and fare policy, and puts state solid-waste policy under its Superintendencia de Planejamento e Gestao Territorial.

Committee for Roads of the Republic of K.desc: A committee inside the Kazakh government ministry that holds roads, at present the Ministry of Transport. Government Resolution 1193 of 6 December 2007 gave it its present name, renaming the Committee for Development of Transport Infrastructure of the then Ministry of Transport and Communications and listing it among that ministry's subordinate departments; a 2016 ministerial order names it as a committee of the Ministry of Investments and Development. Its areas of work are road construction and reconstruction, road repair and maintenance, the local road network and toll roads, and it approves the yearly investment plan of the national road operator.

KazAvtoZhol.desc: A state-owned joint stock company in Kazakhstan, KazAvtoZhol National Company JSC, established in 2013 under the Ministry of Transport. It is the national operator of the main national road network, including international transit roads; its annual investment plan has to be approved by the Roads Committee, and it manages and collects toll revenue through its KazToll portal.

Department of Public Works and Highways.desc: A department of the Philippine national government. Its mandate, which its own site takes from section 3 of Executive Order 124 of 1987, is the planning, design, construction and maintenance of infrastructure facilities, especially national highways, flood control and water resource development systems, and other public works. Below the Office of the Secretary it has undersecretaries and assistant secretaries, bureaus, regional offices in Luzon and in the Visayas and Mindanao, and a Unified Project Management Office with five specialised clusters.

Hanoi People's Committee.desc: The executive body of Hanoi's People's Council and the city's local state administrative body. Under Vietnam's 2015 Law on Organization of Local Administration a People's Committee is elected by the People's Council at the same level and is made up of a chairperson, vice chairpersons and members, with at most five vice chairpersons for Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City. As the committee of a centrally run city it draws up land-use and urban-planning contents for its People's Council to decide, carries them out, and builds and manages the city's urban infrastructure works.

sources.title: Law No. 77/2015/QH13 on Organization of Local Administration

Hanoi Department of Transport.desc: A specialised agency of the Hanoi People's Committee. Under the committee's Decision 17/2008/QD-UBND of 29 September 2008 it advises and assists the committee in state management of transport in the city, covering roads, waterways and urban railways. A 2015 joint circular of the transport and home affairs ministries puts its organisation, staffing and activities under the direction of the provincial people's committee and its technical work under the guidance of the Ministry of Transport.

sources.title: Hanoi Urban Railway Construction Project, preparatory survey report

TRAMOC (Hanoi Public Transport Managemen.desc: A unit under the Hanoi Department of Transport, established by Hanoi People's Committee Decision 2279/QD-UBND of 31 May 2007 to assist what was then the Department of Transport and Public Works in managing and monitoring public works in the city. Its listed duties include printing and issuing bus tickets and managing the subsidy and the revenue of public transport.

Development Organization for the Rural P.desc: A national non-governmental organisation in Bangladesh, which gives its own name as Development Organisation of the Rural Poor. Its fields of work include water and sanitation, food and agriculture, fisheries, microfinance, women's empowerment, child rights, and mother and child health. Its own site says it works in 31 upazilas across 19 districts, with more than 500 staff and more than 50 workplaces.

Electricity Generation Company of Bangla.desc: A Bangladeshi state electricity generation company under the Power Division of the Ministry of Power, Energy and Mineral Resources. It was incorporated on 23 November 1996 as Meghnaghat Power Company Limited and renamed Electricity Generation Company of Bangladesh Limited on 16 February 2004. It is a public limited company whose shares are not publicly traded, and its 2023 annual report gives its generation capacity as 954 MW across three plants.

Gas Transmission Company Limited (GTCL).desc: A Bangladeshi gas pipeline company, described in its own reports as a company of Petrobangla, the state oil, gas and mineral corporation, which sits under the Ministry of Energy, Power and Mineral Resources. It takes gas into the pipelines it operates and delivers it on. Its revenue was more than 22.67 billion taka in the 2024-25 financial year, with net profit after tax of more than 2.46 billion taka.

Power Grid Company of Bangladesh (PGCB).desc: The company that carries high-voltage electricity across Bangladesh, wheeling power from Bangladesh Power Development Board stations and other generating companies to the distribution utilities at a charge fixed by the Bangladesh Electricity Regulatory Commission. It is a public limited company whose memorandum, signed on 18 November 1996, was subscribed by the state-owned Bangladesh Power Development Board; it was listed in 2006 when that board sold a 15.36 per cent stake, and sponsors and directors still held 80.10 per cent of the shares in February 2021. Its network included 2,407 circuit km of 400 kV line and 8,445 circuit km of 132 kV line up to March 2024, and its name was changed to Power Grid Bangladesh PLC by a resolution of 10 February 2024.

Ghana Water Company Limited (GWCL).desc: Ghana's urban water utility, a wholly state-owned limited liability company that abstracts, treats and supplies drinking water to urban communities and plans and develops urban water supply systems. It was created on 1 July 1999 by converting the Ghana Water and Sewerage Corporation, which Parliament had set up by Act 310 of 1965, under the Statutory Corporations (Conversion to Companies) Act 461 of 1993 as amended by LI 1648. Ghana's state holding agency, SIGA, lists it as 100 per cent state-owned; Ghana News Agency reports in 2025 and 2026 call it Ghana Water Limited (GWL).

Maîtrise d'Ouvrage de l'Aéroport de Dons.desc: A Burkinabe public body that ran the building of the new Ouagadougou-Donsin airport, headed by a director general appointed by the Council of Ministers. Its 2019 tender documents were issued under the Prime Minister's Office, and the airport project moved from there to the Ministry of Transport on 13 April 2022. In June 2025 the Council of Ministers adopted a decree creating a state company, the Société des Aéroports du Faso, which takes over MOAD's functions along with those of two other aviation bodies.

Intercontinental Consultants and Technoc.desc: An engineering consultancy registered in India, incorporated in 1987 and started from a modest set-up in New Delhi. Highways are its largest line of work, accounting for more than 80 per cent of revenue in the years to 2018; it also works on bridges and tunnels, traffic and road safety, rail and metro, airports, urban planning, water resources and environmental and social studies. A credit rating report put its operating income at 278.8 crore rupees in the 2017-18 financial year, on provisional results.

NTPC Limited.desc: India's state-controlled electricity generation company, incorporated on 7 November 1975 as National Thermal Power Corporation Private Ltd and renamed NTPC Limited on 28 October 2005. The Government of India holds 51.10 per cent of its equity, it was given Maharatna status in May 2010, and its shares have been listed since November 2004. Its own figures put the NTPC group at 91,668 MW of installed capacity across 119 plants in November 2026, of which 60,992 MW is in NTPC's own plants, most of it coal-fired, and put the company at 17 per cent of India's total national capacity as of 31 March 2026.
